headline: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz in 7 days. It has conditions.
summary: Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, laid out the offer in New York on Thursday, one attendee said. Iran reopens the Strait of Hormuz and restarts nuclear talks in seven days. In return the US lifts its naval blockade, waives sanctions on Iranian oil and holds a ceasefire that covers Lebanon. A similar deal in June quickly collapsed.

cover_question.q: Can you really close the sea?

cover_answer: One narrow gap of it. Iran's been attacking ships there.
table_question: Would you make a deal with someone who broke the last one?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: There's a narrow gap of sea near a country called Iran where the big oil ships go through. Iran has been attacking ships there, so they stopped going. Now Iran says it will open the gap in seven days if America does some things first. It's like two kids blocking a door and each one saying you move first. The grown-ups are talking.
5-7.why: One gap, one door, two kids who won't move. The war stays out of it.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script gives them a door with two kids in it, a standoff they have stood in themselves. The gap of sea is the one concrete fact; the blockade, the sanctions and the ceasefire stay with the grown-ups. Expect "who moves first?" Nobody has yet, and that is the whole story.

8-12.script: Iran attacked ships in the Strait of Hormuz, and gas prices jumped. The US blockaded Iran. Now Iran offers: in seven days it reopens the strait if the US lifts the blockade, waives oil sanctions and holds a ceasefire. A card trade: neither kid hands over first.
8-12.why: Ship, pump, blockade, offer: one chain. The card trade is the standoff.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out chains of cause and effect, so the script runs one from a ship to a gas pump to a blockade to an offer, then hands them the standoff as a card trade, a deal they have refused themselves. Both sides want the other to let go first. Expect "why not just say yes?" A deal like it in June quickly fell apart.

13-17.script: Would you take a deal from someone who broke the last one? In June the two sides agreed a 60-day version; it collapsed when Iran hit ships again. Second: Trita Parsi says a fast deal helps Trump before the midterms. Should an election clock end a war?
13-17.why: Two arguable questions. June is the fact they have to reckon with.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things: a deal that collapsed once can still be the least bad option, and a peace that arrives on an election timetable is still a peace. The script gives them June as the fact and Parsi's midterm point as the motive. Expect "so is the war ending?" Nobody said that. Iran offered. Trump says he is in no rush.

5-7.q: Can you really close the sea?
5-7.a: Not the whole sea. One narrow gap where the big oil ships go. Iran attacked ships there, so they stopped going.

8-12.q: Why does Iran want the ships to move now?
8-12.a: Its economy is hurting under the US blockade and oil sanctions. Reopening sells its oil, and Trump gets cheaper gas before an election.

8-12.q: What does the US have to give?
8-12.a: Lift the naval blockade, waive sanctions on Iranian oil and hold a ceasefire that includes Lebanon. Then nuclear talks restart.

13-17.q: Why would Trump say no to cheaper gas?
13-17.a: He says he's in no rush. Parsi warns Iran may just be buying time to sell more oil. Neither side wants to give up leverage.
Qatar carries messages between them; Iran's president met its prime minister Friday. Rubio says the US will exchange ideas if there's a chance.
